title: Fractional batching -> kernel misalignment postmortem & rollout playbook
creator: Marcus Li
description: Summary: A recent deploy that introduced fractional batching heuristics (aimed at improving GPU utilization for small requests) produced a spike in p99 latency for mixed-sequence workloads. The high-level symptom was long tail latency on chat-style sessions (>1024 tokens) where previously-stable traffic saw sporadic 5-10x p99 regressions for ~6 hours. This ticket documents the timeline, diagnostic findings, immediate mitigations, and a playbook for safe rollout of batching/scheduler heuristics.
impact_summary: Customer-facing latency regressions (p99) for hosted API across regions us-east and eu-west for ~6 hours. ~0.6% of requests experienced >2s additional latency; no data loss, no request failures. Several customers with strict latency SLOs contacted support. Estimated revenue exposure low but developer trust impact medium.
timeline: 2026-03-10 01:12 UTC: New heuristic (fractional_batching_v2) merged to runtime main and rolled to canary cluster.
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC: Canary metrics show CPU/GPU efficiency improvement but p99 jitter increases on canary traffic. Rollout continues per automated gate (false negative on our p99 alert).
2026-03-10 03:50 UTC: Full roll started to production (automated); first incident reports from SRE at 04:10 UTC.
2026-03-10 04:15 UTC: Pager triggered for p99 > 750ms on text-generation route. Initial rollback attempt failed due to sticky autoscaler state on some hosts.
2026-03-10 05:05 UTC: Hotfix: disable fractional_batching_v2 flag globally; scheduler reverted to previous heuristic. p99 gradually returned to baseline by 06:30 UTC.
2026-03-10 08:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved; post-incident analysis started.
2026-03-11 to 2026-03-13: Deep dive diagnostics and synthetic repro runs completed.
root_cause: Interaction between fractional batching and the kernel selection path for quantized attention kernels. Fractional batching introduced micro-batches with token-length padding patterns that misaligned with the kernel's expected tile boundaries (tile-size=32 in quantized attention path). That misalignment caused the kernel selector to choose a slower fallback kernel for roughly 1 in 160 requests when sequence length crossed specific thresholds, which dramatically increased compute time and caused KV cache churn because of unexpected cache invalidations from micro-batch boundary conditions.
mitigation_actions: Immediate: Rollback fractional_batching_v2 flag (done by 2026-03-10 05:05 UTC).
Short-term: Add a guard in scheduler to disable fractional batching for quantized-attn models and sequences > 1024 tokens (release runtime-1.23-hotfix, target 2026-03-15).
Medium-term: Update kernel selector to consider padding alignment (tile boundary aware) and prefer aligned kernels or insert low-cost padding to avoid fallback kernel (refactor PR #8721).

Long-term: Add unit and chaos tests: synthetic mixed-sequence load tests that exercise small + long chat sessions with quantized models in CI. Add a regression sentinel in canary gating that simulates the mixed workload (dashboard + automated gate).
Observability: Add a metric for 'kernel-selector-fallback-rate' and a KV cache invalidation counter per host (Grafana dashboard and alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m).
Process: Update rollout policy to require explicit p99 canary verification for deployment bundles that touch scheduler/kernel-selector heuristics.
